issues.issue: The definition says the Lenders "become a party" to a Common Project Financing Facility that "may be subject to an Intercreditor Agreement," without stating how or on whose consent that happens. The permissive "may" leaves the pari passu ranking it promises without any enforcement mechanism.

The term sweeps in "the executed documents included by or on behalf of the Borrower in the IntraLinks electronic data site" with no list or index, so what is Confidential Information Material (and hence a Disclosed Matter) cannot be fixed from the instrument. The carve-out proviso further disclaims the very representations the definition otherwise imports.

The proviso lets the Borrower and a counterparty substitute Minnesota or foreign governing law into a Consent and Agreement "without the consent of the Required Lenders or the Security Agent being required," which does not square with the Additional Security Documents and Security Documents definitions requiring security instruments to be satisfactory to the Security Agent. It also sits uneasily with the Section 9.02 amendment machinery for Loan Documents.

"Control" turns on the power to direct "the management or policies of a Person ... by contract or otherwise," a formula with no ownership or voting threshold. Whether a lender's covenant rights or a shareholder agreement confers Control cannot be answered from the words.

"Other assets that are due, or likely to be converted into cash, sold, exchanged, or expensed in the normal course of business, within one (1) year" turns on the vague test "likely," with no probability standard or measurer. Because the Security Agreement subordinates the Lenders' interest in Current Assets to a Working Capital Bank, the boundary matters.

Clause (c) captures "all scheduled amortization repayments of any other Indebtedness" without saying what it is "other" than, given that clause (a) covers finance charges and clause (b) lease principal. The scope of the residual category is left to inference.

"Any matters disclosed in the Confidential Information Material" makes the disclosure exception co-extensive with an undelimited data room and an information memorandum prepared by a third party. What has been disclosed, and therefore excepted from the representations, cannot be determined from the text.

The add-back for "any items treated as exceptional or extraordinary items" does not say by whom they are so treated and, unlike Adjusted Net Income, does not distinguish gains from losses. The same items are already excluded at the Adjusted Net Income stage, so the add-back's operation is uncertain.

The definition points to "the Guarantee Agreement," singular, while the Agreement defines only "Guarantee Agreements" — two separate documents in the forms of Exhibits E-1 and E-2. The release date is in fact defined only in the EGL Guarantee Agreement, and that document conditions it on offtake agreements approved by 66 2/3% of Term Loan Exposure, a standard found nowhere in this Agreement.

A replacement consultant need only be an "independent, professional and reputable engineering firm appointed," without saying who appoints it or on what standard of acceptance. The cross-reference is also left incomplete as "Section 5.04(b".

The Environmental Consultant is simply "such independent, professional and reputable environmental advisory firm appointed," naming no firm and no appointing party. The qualifying adjectives supply no measurable standard.

After naming four specific contracts the definition adds "any other material contract entered into by the Borrower with respect to any engineering, procurement or construction services in connection with the Project." The catch-all uses an undefined materiality test and invites an ejusdem generis dispute about its reach.

The Escrow Account is to receive "all Cash and receivables arising out of any contracts of the Borrower ... or payments otherwise received by Borrower, to be applied in accordance with the Cash Sweep Mechanism," which cannot be squared with Section 2.05, under which the Escrow Agent makes funds available to the Borrower for the purposes in its Borrowing Request. The Cash Sweep Mechanism governs only sweep payments and supplies no application rule for ordinary receipts.

The definition contemplates "any successor collateral agent appointed pursuant to the Collateral Account Agreement," although the collateral agent role belongs to the separately defined Security Agent and no "collateral agent" is defined. The mismatch leaves it unclear whose successor is meant.

The definition says the term "refers to whether such Loan ... are bearing interest at a rate determined by reference to the LIBO Rate," which defines a category by posing a question rather than by fixing a class. It also mismatches singular and plural subjects.

Clause (ii) turns on withholding Tax imposed "under any Laws in effect at the time such recipient acquires its ownership interest," using a capitalized "Laws" that the Agreement never defines. Whether it means only tax laws of a particular jurisdiction is left open.

The definition omits its operative verb: "\"Existing Credit Agreement\" the Credit Agreement dated September 22, 2010 between the Borrower and Union Bank of India." As written it is a fragment rather than a definition.

The FACR numerator counts fixed assets over which the Secured Parties hold a first priority security interest "(subject only to Permitted Liens thereon)", but "Permitted Liens" is not a defined term in this Agreement, which defines "Permitted Encumbrances" instead. The denominator likewise refers to an "Upstream Supplier Project Financing Creditor," a term that appears nowhere else.

Financial Closure requires Total Commitments aggregating US$530,000,000, but the Total Commitment definition fixes the commitment at US$250,000,000 unless Subsequent Project Lenders accede under Section 2.20, which no one is obliged to procure. Availability of Initial Lender Tranche B under Section 2.02(b) and the fixing of the Scheduled Commercial Operations Date both hang on a condition that may be incapable of satisfaction.

The enumerated events close with "or other similar acts beyond the reasonable control of the Borrower," a general catch-all after a list of specifics that raises an ejusdem generis question about its reach. Whether things such as supplier insolvency or regulatory delay qualify is not answerable from the list.

"Related proceedings thereto that may be filed elsewhere in Federal or state court" has no boundary of subject matter, party or time. Because the Great Lakes Litigation is carved out of the representations and defaults, the width of "related proceedings" is consequential.
